text: Evaluate, multiply, interpolate; the butterfly.
coefficients values at ωᵏ product values FFT multiply inverse FFT: back to coefficients

Multiplying two polynomials of degree n directly is O(n²). But a polynomial of degree < N is fixed by its values at N points, and values multiply point by point. So: evaluate both at N special points, multiply the values, and turn the products back into coefficients. FFT (快速傅里叶变换) does the evaluation and its inverse in O(N log N).

The special points are the N-th roots of unity ωk. Splitting A(x) = Aeven(x²) + x·Aodd(x²) halves the problem, because the squares of the N roots are the N/2 roots, each twice. The inverse transform is the same algorithm with ω⁻¹, divided by N.
(1 + 2x)(1 + 2x + x²) = 1 + 4x + 5x² + 2x³ (P3803). The size N must be a power of two of at least n + m + 1, and results are rounded with llround because doubles carry small errors.

Floating-point FFT loses precision when coefficients or N are large (products near 10¹⁵ and beyond). For exact answers modulo a prime, use NTT (8.2); for an arbitrary modulus, split numbers into 15-bit halves or use three NTT primes (P4245).
NTT mod 998244353; big-number multiplication.
NTT (快速数论变换) is FFT done modulo a prime p = c·2k + 1, such as 998244353 = 119·2²³ + 1. A primitive root g (3 for 998244353) gives g(p−1)/N, which behaves exactly like an N-th root of unity mod p.
Same code, integer arithmetic, no rounding errors.

Convolution is everywhere: big-number multiplication (digits as coefficients, P1919), counting pairs with a given sum, matching with wildcards, and the "force" sums of P3338 after reversing one array. Whenever ck = Σi+j=k aibj appears, think convolution.
Each digit position of the product is a convolution of digits, at most 9·9·(length) ≈ 8·10⁷ for 10⁶ digits, safely below the prime, so the result is exact. Carries are handled once at the end.
The second test is checked against Python's exact big-integer product. Reverse the strings so index i is the 10i digit, and strip leading zeros (but keep one for a product of 0).

Further polynomial tools Idea divide-and-conquer FFT (分治 FFT, P4721) f[i] = Σ f[j]g[i−j] with f on both sides: CDQ, each half convolved once polynomial inverse (P4238) Newton iteration doubling the precision: B ← B(2 − AB) circular / correlation sums (P3723 礼物) reverse one array and double the other, read the needed coefficients repeated convolution (P3321) fast power of a polynomial, NTT inside
The Luogu problems for this chapter, a ladder through them, and experiments to try yourself.
Key points to memorise
1. Values at N points determine a degree < N polynomial; values multiply pointwise.
2. FFT: split even / odd; roots of unity square to half as many roots; O(N log N).
3. Iterative: bit-reversal order, then butterflies u ± w·v for len = 2, 4, ….
4. Inverse: ω⁻¹ and divide by N. N = power of two ≥ n + m + 1.
5. NTT: p = 998244353, g = 3, root g^((p−1)/len); exact, no rounding.
6. c_k = Σ_{i+j=k} a_i b_j ⇒ convolution; reverse an array for differences i − j.
